chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad) from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Abu al-Subbah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the mukatab (slave who has contracted for manumission for a specified sum), if he pays half of his manumission money and the half remains upon him, then he calls his masters to the remainder of his manumission and says: 'Take what remains as a single payment.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They take what remains, then he is freed.'

And he said regarding the mukatab who pays part of his manumission money, then dies, leaving a son and wealth greater than what he owes from his manumission: 'He pays his masters what remains of his manumission, and what remains is for his son.'

key_terms.المُكَاتَب: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom in installments
key_terms.مَوَالِيَهُ: His masters (plural of mawla, referring to the owner(s) of the slave)
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The manumission contract or the agreed-upon sum for freedom

ai.seo_question: How is the remaining manumission debt handled if a mukatab slave dies leaving surplus wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the procedural mechanics of *kitabah*, emphasizing that the master's consent to accept the remainder in a single payment triggers immediate emancipation, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence. It further establishes the priority of debt settlement over inheritance, ensuring that the mukatab's estate first covers the outstanding manumission balance before the surplus passes to his heir, reflecting the principle of settling obligations prior to distribution.
